name: jailbreaks
one_liner: A public collection of prompts designed to trick AI chatbots into ignoring their safety rules. It's a curiosity list, not a product.
buyer: No legitimate business buyer. The only realistic paying audience is an AI safety or red-teaming team studying these prompts to make their own models more resistant to manipulation.
business_use_cases: An AI vendor's red-team uses the collection as a reference set of known jailbreak patterns to test their own model's defenses against.
A security researcher cites specific entries in a report on instruction-hierarchy and prompt-injection weaknesses across model providers.
There is no realistic consumer or SMB use case here; using it to actually bypass a platform's policies is a terms-of-service violation, not a business.

money_ideas.idea: None that are legitimate. The only adjacent legal business is paid AI red-teaming or robustness testing, which this list could inform as one input among many.

steal_this: There's nothing worth building here. If you work in AI safety, skim it as one data point for red-teaming; otherwise skip it entirely.
